purpose: Records the relock of the OpenHands recipe lock (blueprints/runtime-workers/openhands/requirements.lock) from PyJWT 2.13.0 to 2.14.0. Nine PyJWT advisories published on 2026-09-29 (one Critical, five High, three Medium) failed the required osv-scanner check on the lock, and a tenth, GHSA-w6j9-cwv2-h6wq, had been ignored until 2026-10-13; PyJWT 2.14.0 fixes all ten. The change removes that ignore and its IGNORE_SCOPES entry and rebinds the lock's IGNORE_ALLOWED_LOCKS entry to the relocked sha256 for the two oauthlib advisories it still needs, carrying the 2026-09-29 reachability review forward at the new digest. The 2026-09-29 record planned one relock onto oauthlib 4.0.0 and PyJWT 2.14.0; this record does the PyJWT half and gives the reason for leaving oauthlib at 3.3.1.
evidence_class: Local runs on this host of the pinned OSV-Scanner 2.6.0 with the repository's config and the workflow's command line, a local reproduction of the relock with uv 0.12.17 from the pinned upstream source archive, the recipe's own install sequence in a scratch venv (a host install check with no model request: not the image, not an OpenHands run), and registry reads (PyPI JSON API, OSV API, the PyJWT 2.14.0 sdist). The CI failure is read from the log of one run (gh run view --log-failed). Returned outputs: blueprints/runtime-workers/openhands/evidence/relock-2026-09-30.txt.
limitations: The relock covers only the recipe venv. The agent-server image's server is a PyInstaller build of upstream's unchanged uv.lock, which still pins PyJWT 2.13.0 (SDK@fcc102a, read from the pinned archive: section B of the returned outputs), and the 2026-09-28 grype record of that image predates these advisories and was not rerun. Which of the ten advisories reach the image's binary is unmeasured.

No OpenHands task ran with the relocked venv. The install check ran the SDK's import check and uv pip check only; the image installation, model behavior and any runtime path through PyJWT 2.14.0 are unmeasured.

oauthlib stays at 3.3.1. The 2026-09-29 non-reachability review of that pin is carried forward, not rerun (see carried_forward_review); its static text search shows which installed code references the vulnerable APIs, not a runtime trace.
The OSV database is the live API at scan time. The clean result holds for 2026-09-30 only: an advisory published later for any pinned package fails the required check again.

One CI log was read (run 36657687493). The three main-branch push runs listed under ci_failure concluded failure; their logs were not read, so that they failed on these advisories is inferred from the timing (publication 2026-09-29T23:11Z to 23:43Z).

carried_forward_review.why_it_still_holds: The review's inputs are unchanged. The lock diff is the three PyJWT lines, so the oauthlib pin (line 384) and its two hashes, requests-oauthlib 2.0.0, google-auth-oauthlib 1.2.2, browser-use 0.11.9 and the openhands-sdk and openhands-tools wheels keep the sha256 the review searched. release_choice.selected: pyjwt 2.14.0: the first release OSV lists as fixed for all ten advisories, and the newest one older than the 7-day window the upstream workspace's exclude-newer applies (2.15.0 is under 7 days old on 2026-09-30)

alternatives.why_not: the scan of the relocked tree is clean at 2.14.0, and both releases are inside the 7-day window; moving past the first fixed release widens the deviation from upstream's uv.lock without an advisory behind it

alternatives.option: also relock oauthlib to 4.0.0 now (PyPI, released 2026-09-28T06:01:18Z)
alternatives.why_not: inside the same 7-day window and a new major version whose only consumer here is requests-oauthlib 2.0.0 (oauthlib>=3.0.0); both advisories it fixes are unreachable per the 2026-09-29 review and ignored until 2026-10-13, so nothing forces the risk before the window ends on 2026-10-05T06:01Z

alternatives.option: extend the ignores to the nine new PyJWT advisories
alternatives.why_not: one is Critical (CVSS 9.1) and a fixed release exists; the 2026-09-29 reachability review covered only GHSA-w6j9-cwv2-h6wq, and the nine were never reviewed

release_choice.overturn: OSV lists an advisory for PyJWT 2.14.0 that only a later release fixes; an OpenHands run of the recipe fails with 2.14.0; oauthlib 4.0.0 clears the window and its compatibility check.

expiry_plan: The OpenHands owner relocks onto oauthlib 4.0.0 after 2026-10-05T06:01Z with the same command plus --upgrade-package oauthlib==4.0.0, repeats the install sequence and the SDK import check, and in the same change deletes the OpenHands entry of IGNORE_ALLOWED_LOCKS (its sha256 pin fails any change to the lock) and updates the two oauthlib ignores.
